compiled_state.title: As a brainstorm scrutiny pipeline, the scenario red team detects unspoken premises via the assumption category
compiled_state.author: Test
compiled_state.description:
## Description

**What**: Add a 4th `assumption` category to plugins/dso/skills/brainstorm/prompts/scenario-red-team.md with 4 sub-bullets, co-located scope parentheticals, and an inverted 4-step decision tree (fire-first ordering). Update the JSON output schema's `category` enum to include `"assumption"`.

**Why**: This is the downstream catch at the scenario-red-team layer. Closes the meta-blind-spot the bot-psychologist identified in brainstorm: prior designs used suppress-first decision trees and judgment-based criteria; the inverted tree grounds LLM behavior in observable evidence.

**Scope**:
- IN: 4-sub-bullet `assumption` category (Inputs-and-data; User and actor model; Operating environment and scale; Trust and authority boundaries); co-located scope parentheticals (sub-bullet 1: "(applies regardless of whether the sourcing mechanism is also covered in the Approach section)"); inverted 4-step decision tree (Step 1 fires Inputs-and-data; Step 2 requires verified true to suppress with MUST-execute Read/Grep; Step 3 requires verbatim match in `explicit` SC; Step 4 requires specific-claim conventional default with established domain); schema enum addition `"assumption"` matching sub-bullet 1 category name.
- OUT: Blue-team prompt changes (existing filter rubric covers); changes to dso:red-team-reviewer agent (different agent, c183-ed2a).

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, plugins/dso/skills/brainstorm/prompts/scenario-red-team.md contains the assumption category with 4 sub-bullets and co-located scope parentheticals, verified by structural test asserting the canonical category heading and sub-bullet markers are present.
  ← Satisfies: "Cross-file structural consistency"
- When this story is complete, the inverted 4-step decision tree is documented in the assumption-category section with the canonical Step 1-4 phrasing (fire-first ordering, MUST-execute Read/Grep, verbatim-match requirement, specific-claim conventional default), verified by structural test on the canonical step phrases.
  ← Satisfies: "Cross-file structural consistency"
- When this story is complete, the JSON output schema's `category` enum includes the literal string `"assumption"` and matches the sub-bullet 1 category name documented in the file, verified by structural test asserting the enum value is present in the schema definition AND in scenario-red-team.md.
  ← Satisfies: "Schema, marker, and rendering integration"
- When this story is complete, synthetic brainstorm cases verify the decision tree across 7 sub-cases (a-g per epic SC3), each producing the expected fire/suppress verdict.
  ← Satisfies: "Decision-tree calibration replay"

## Considerations

- [Maintainability] Schema enum change to `category` field affects red-team output validation; ensure schema migration is documented and downstream consumers (blue-team-filter agent) handle the new enum value.
- [Testing] Structural tests assert canonical phrases are present, not full content match (change-detector resistance).
- [Reliability] 5-second Read/Grep timeout in Step 2 must fail closed.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
